title: Hot-path query plans

metrics.reason: Postgres planner cost units (EXPLAIN's arbitrary 'Total Cost'), not milliseconds or a comparable-across-databases number — informational trend only, per design SS4.7 ('per-query estimated cost as info').

notes: No Postgres in this authoring container at build time, but VERIFIED END-TO-END against a real migrated+seeded Postgres later in the same task (a cluster another builder left running at 127.0.0.1:5432/visionquest_local) — self-test reported seq_scans_on_large_tables=0, plans_captured=26, avg_estimated_cost=1.96 over the real cohort. requires: ["postgres","cohort"], checked via DATABASE_URL; runs in CI's hermetic pgvector service inside the `bench -- --tier=gate --compare` step, seeded via scripts/bench/seed-cohort.ts (see ci.yml). Captures the REAL SQL Prisma emits for six hot queries (the task's five plus a second dashboard-bundle read) via a purpose-built PrismaClient with query-event logging, using production pure-helpers/constants for the where/select shape wherever exported (LEAD_LIST_SELECT, interventionQueueStudentSelect, buildManagedStudentWhere, connectManagedStudentIds, reportDateRangeBoundsUtc, intersectScopeClassIds) rather than hand-writing SQL — see the scorer's header for why db.ts itself was not touched (shared, RLS-security-relevant, out of this suite's ownership) and how identical Prisma call arguments produce identical SQL regardless of which client instance issues them. interventionQueueStudentSelect lives in src/lib/teacher/intervention-queue-select.ts (moved out of dashboard.ts, which opens with `import "server-only"` and throws for any importer outside a Next.js server-component context — this scorer is a plain script and hit that throw on the first real run before the move). plans_captured=26 across 6 named hot-query call sites is expected, not a bug: Prisma decomposes a findMany with several to-many relations (the intervention queue's select nests 12) into one SQL statement per relation rather than a single JOIN, so this number is itself real evidence about relational fan-out, not an artifact. 'Large table' is gated by ACTUAL row count (pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup after an explicit ANALYZE, threshold 10,000) rather than by table name, because the 50-student synthetic cohort has no table anywhere near that size — gating by name alone would flag Postgres's normal, correct choice to Seq Scan a tiny table; a meaningful non-trivial signal needs a larger seed, a follow-up left for the coordinator/database-architect rather than invented here by faking scale. The verification connection used the Postgres superuser role, which bypasses RLS entirely (the standing 'local dev connects as postgres' characteristic) — connectManagedStudentIds's own internal query therefore ran unscoped by RLS during this check; that call is qualifying data for the funnel query's parameters, not one of the six captured hot queries itself, so the captured SQL/plans are unaffected, but a CI run with RLS actually enforced has not been separately confirmed. plans_captured now carries floor:1/direction:higher (was floor:null/INFO) so a total EXPLAIN failure — every hot query erroring before a single plan is captured — fails the gate instead of reading as merely informational; buildHotQueries() now accepts an optional `studentIds` override so its descriptor-building logic is unit-tested without a database (query-plans.test.mjs), and is called exactly once per run (it previously ran a second time only to count its own length).
